datadog-mcp-api.$comment: Identifies requests to the Datadog hosted MCP server (mcp.datadoghq.com and the regional hosts mcp.us3/us5/ap1/ap2/uk1.datadoghq.com and mcp.datadoghq.eu).

datadog-mcp-session.$comment: Open and maintain an MCP session: initialize, list tools/prompts/resources, ping, and send notifications. Required for any MCP client to function; does not read or modify Datadog content.

datadog-mcp-read-all.$comment: Run any read-only Datadog MCP tool (logs, metrics, traces, infrastructure, monitors, incidents, dashboards, security, RUM, CI, feature flags, LLM observability, DDSQL queries, documentation and other lookups) plus the MCP session handshake. Covers all toolsets, including the preview ones.

datadog-mcp-write-all.$comment: Run any Datadog MCP tool that creates, modifies, deletes, triggers or executes something (monitors, dashboards, notebooks, cases, security rules, log configuration, workflows, agents, feature flags, experiments, sandboxed code, remote actions and more) plus the MCP session handshake. Covers all toolsets, including the preview ones.

datadog-mcp-read-telemetry.$comment: See the monitoring data Datadog has collected about your systems: logs, events and Audit Trail, metrics, traces and spans, service health and the Software Catalog, profiles, Live Debugger snapshots, hosts, processes, Kubernetes and cloud resources, network monitoring, Database Monitoring, Cloud Cost recommendations, and the configuration of log pipelines, indexes and archives. Also lets the agent run read-only DDSQL queries across that data and read saved DDSQL queries. (Includes the legacy get_logs and search_datadog_services names.)

datadog-mcp-write-telemetry-configuratio.$comment: Change how Datadog collects, processes and stores monitoring data: create, update, reorder or delete log pipelines, indexes and archives, create Observability Pipelines, manage derived metrics and metric tag configuration, create or delete APM sampling and service-remapping rules, enable Live Debugger and create or disable logpoints, create Reference Tables and add rows to them, and save DDSQL queries. Does not change anything on the monitored hosts themselves.

datadog-mcp-read-user-experience.$comment: See how real users experience your applications: Real User Monitoring events, applications, views and operations, Session Replay recordings and summaries, Product Analytics (funnels, pathways, retention), and Error Tracking issues and their analytics.

datadog-mcp-write-user-experience.$comment: Change Real User Monitoring and Error Tracking settings and triage: create, update or delete RUM operations, custom RUM metrics and retention filters, and change the state, assignee, comments and Jira/Linear/case links of Error Tracking issues.

datadog-mcp-read-monitoring-and-incident.$comment: See how problems are detected and handled: monitors, monitor groups, templates and coverage gaps, SLOs, incidents, Bits AI investigations and their findings, Watchdog anomalies and forecasts, external provider outages, Work Management cases and projects, and Datadog user lookups. Also validates monitor definitions without saving them.

datadog-mcp-write-monitoring-and-inciden.$comment: Create monitors (in draft mode), trigger and steer Bits AI investigations for alerts and incidents, and manage Work Management cases: create and update cases and projects, add comments and attachments, and link cases to each other or to Jira issues.

datadog-mcp-read-dashboards.$comment: See dashboards, notebooks, widgets and Datadog spreadsheets: search and fetch them, render and verify widgets, validate widget and notebook cell definitions, and consult widget-building reference material.

datadog-mcp-write-dashboards.$comment: Create, update, restore or delete dashboards, notebooks and Datadog spreadsheets.

datadog-mcp-read-security-and-governance.$comment: See security and organization governance data: security signals, findings and threat indicators, detection rules, suppressions and automation rules, App & API Protection passlists, denylists, custom WAF rules and blocking configuration, Infrastructure as Code custom rules, governance insights, controls, detections, limits, best practices and tag rules. Also scans code for hardcoded secrets and drafts or validates IaC rules without saving them.

datadog-mcp-write-security-and-governanc.$comment: Change security and governance configuration and triage: triage signals and threat indicators, create, update or delete detection rules, suppressions and findings automation rules, mute, assign, re-prioritize or ticket findings, manage App & API Protection passlists, denylists and custom WAF rules, create, publish or delete Infrastructure as Code custom rules, mitigate governance detections, and create, update or delete tag rules.

datadog-mcp-read-software-delivery.$comment: See how software is built, tested and shipped: CI pipelines, test runs and flaky tests, code coverage, DORA deployment metrics, Deployment Gates, Synthetic tests, feature flags and their allocations, flag usage in code, and experiments with their results and diagnostics.

datadog-mcp-write-software-delivery.$comment: Quarantine or disable flaky tests, create or edit Synthetic HTTP API tests, create feature flags and change their per-environment configuration and allocations, and create, start, conclude or cancel experiments.

datadog-mcp-read-data-and-llm-observabil.$comment: See data pipeline and AI application monitoring: the data catalog with entity details, lineage and tags, warehouse query history, data quality monitors and coverage, Spark job health, and LLM Observability traces and spans, agent loops and insights, experiments, evaluators and evaluations, projects, datasets, Patterns results and annotation queues.

datadog-mcp-write-data-and-llm-observabi.$comment: Change data catalog and LLM Observability content: set tags and descriptions on data entities, create LLM experiments, update insight status and submit feedback, create, update or delete evaluators, add dataset records, create or update Patterns configurations and trigger Patterns runs, and manage annotation queues, label schemas and annotations.

datadog-mcp-read-automation.$comment: See Workflow Automation workflows, their actions and execution history, Bits AI agents and their conversations, Forms and their responses, and Datadog Assistant conversation history. Also validates workflow definitions without saving them.

datadog-mcp-write-automation.$comment: Create, update, publish, unpublish or delete workflows, create and configure Bits AI agents (including their managed MCP servers), and create, update, publish or clone Forms. Does not execute anything; see run-actions-and-code for that.

datadog-mcp-run-actions-and-code.$comment: Make things happen rather than read or configure them: execute or cancel workflow runs, run Bits AI agents, send messages to the Datadog Assistant, run Network Path traceroutes and restricted read-only shell commands on monitored hosts through a Private Action Runner, and execute agent-written JavaScript in a Datadog-managed sandbox (execute_code), which can read or change any Datadog resource the user has access to. This is the most powerful permission in the set.

datadog-mcp-read-reference.$comment: Look up reference material: search and read Datadog documentation, the code-execution SDK reference and product onboarding guides, and list Reference Tables and read their rows.
